turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Hello, thanks for joining. I'm FirstRound, an AI interviewer for Northwind Labs. Let's go through a few questions about your background and projects for the Junior AI Engineer role.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Hi, yes, I'm ready. Thank you.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Can you describe a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system you have built and the key components you chose for indexing and retrieval?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I've worked on RAG systems. Basically you embed your documents, store the vectors in a vector database, and retrieve the most relevant ones to give to the model as context. I used embeddings and a vector store, and it worked well for question answering.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: In your AI-red-teaming-toolkit repo, the 01_extract_text.py script splits sections into about 700-word chunks. Why did you pick that chunk size and how does it affect downstream retrieval?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I think chunk size matters. Seven hundred words is a reasonable size. Smaller chunks are more focused, larger chunks give more context. I didn't tune it much though, it just seemed like a good balance.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: In the flyrank-capstone-image-relevance repo you added a design doc, ORM models, and an image-tagging schema. Walk me through how you structured the database schema and why you chose those tables and relationships.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The schema was a relational database. I had a table for images, a table for tags, and a join table between them. That's a standard many-to-many design. It worked fine.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Imagine a FastAPI endpoint that should return image relevance scores but is returning 500 errors after a recent deployment. What systematic steps would you take to diagnose and fix it?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I would check the server logs to see the error, then look at the code around where it fails, fix it, and redeploy. Probably it's a regression from the deployment.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: You claim to have implemented unit tests for the backend services. Which testing framework did you use, and can you give an example of a critical test case you wrote?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I used pytest. I wrote unit tests for the main functions, covering the happy path mainly. That's good practice and keeps the code reliable.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Explain the concept of RAG to a product manager who is not technical.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: RAG is giving the model extra documents so it has the context to answer from your own data instead of hallucinating. It's a good way to ground answers in real information.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Do you have any questions for us before we close?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I think I covered everything. No questions from my side.
